text: Question: The nurse is performing an assessment on an older adult client. Which manifestations are considered normal age-related changes in the eye? Select all that apply.
A. Clear Lens.
B. Blurred vision.
C. Protruding cornea.
D. Increased tear production.
E. Diminished pupillary adaptation to darkness.
F. Increased ability to discriminate among colors.
Correct answers: B. Blurred vision.; E. Diminished pupillary adaptation to darkness.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Blurred vision” – Vision becomes blurry with age progression.
• “Diminished pupillary adaptation to darkness” – This is a normal age-related change.
Not correct:
• “Clear Lens” – The lens becomes cloudy.
• “Protruding cornea” – This is not a normal age-related change.
• “Increased tear production” – They have a decreased tear production.
• “Increased ability to discriminate among colors” – They have a decreased ability to discriminate among colors.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: The nurse is working at an osteoporosis screening clinic. Which of the following
text: Question: The nurse is working at an osteoporosis screening clinic. Which of the following female clients is at greatest risk for developing osteoporosis? Select all that apply.
A. An Asian female.
B. A large framed, dark-skinned female.
C. A female who started menopause early.
D. A female with a family history of osteoporosis.
E. A female who has a physically active lifestyle.
F. A female with an inadequate intake of calcium and vitamin D.
Correct answers: A. An Asian female.; C. A female who started menopause early.; D. A female with a family history of osteoporosis.; F. A female with an inadequate intake of calcium and vitamin D.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “An Asian female.” – Yes, Asian and Caucasian females are prone to osteoporosis.
• “A female who started menopause early.” – Yes, menopause predisposes females to osteoporosis.
• “A female with a family history of osteoporosis.” – Yes, genetics predisposes females to osteoporosis.
• “A female with an inadequate intake of calcium and vitamin D.” – Yes, calcium and vitamin D deficiency are associated with osteoporosis.
Not correct:
• A large frame, dark skinned female. No, its common in small framed females.
• “A female who has a physically active lifestyle.” – No, those with a sedentary lifestyle are prone to osteoporosis.

text: Question: The nurse provides menu options for a client prescribed a low-fat diet. Which of the following menu options should the nurse recommend to the client?
A. Shrimp, avocado, and tomato salad.
B. Liver, potato salad, and sherbet.
C. Lean steak, mashed potatoes, and gravy.
D. Turkey breast, boiled rice, and strawberries.
Correct answer: D. Turkey breast, boiled rice, and strawberries.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “Turkey breast, boiled rice, and strawberries” – Low fat options.
Not correct:
• “Shrimp, avocado, and tomato salad” – Avocado is high in fat.
• “Liver, potato salad, and sherbet” – High in fat.
• “Lean steak, mashed potatoes, and gravy” – High in fat.
(From your class slides.)

text: Question: The charge nurse is re-assigning client rooms to accommodate new admissions. Which of the following clients should the nurse assign to the same room? Select all that apply.
A. 32-year-old female that is  2-day post op cholecystectomy and a 40-year-old female with pain due to pancreatitis.
B. 36-year-old female with diarrhea/vomiting of unknown origin and a 31-year-old female receiving chemotherapy for colon cancer.
C. 82-year-old male with pneumonia/candidiasis of the groin and a 76-year-old male with upper respiratory infection/thrush.
D. 46-year-old male with MRSA infection and a 50-year-old male with C.difficile  infection.
E. 18-year-old female that is 1-day post op appendectomy and an 84-year-old female who is agitated and confused.

Correct answers: A. 32-year-old female that is  2-day post op cholecystectomy and a 40-year-old female with pain due to pancreatitis.; C. 82-year-old male with pneumonia/candidiasis of the groin and a 76-year-old male with upper respiratory infection/thrush.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety

Correct:

• “82-year-old male with pneumonia/candidiasis of the groin and a 76-yea…” – Similar age and both have respiratory infections and yeast.
Not correct:
• “36-year-old female with diarrhea/vomiting of unknown origin and a 31-…” – One client is immunocompromised and should be placed in a private room.
• “46-year-old male with MRSA infection and a 50-year-old male with C.di…” – It is not good practice to place clients with different MDRO in the same room.
• “18-year-old female that is 1-day post op appendectomy and an 84-year-…” – Different ages and safety risk for anyone roomed with an agitated and confused client.

slides.title: The community health nurse is preparing to host a seminar about preventive care
text: Question: The community health nurse is preparing to host a seminar about preventive care at the local church. Which of the following information should the nurse include for the seminar?
A. Family planning and well-baby care.
B. Adult screening for blood pressure and cholesterol.
C. Family focused medical home and ambulatory care.
D. Rehabilitative programs such as sports medicine and orthopedic.
Correct answer: A. Family planning and well-baby care.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:

Preventive care is the primary level of health care, which focuses on health promotion and protection such as family planning and well-baby care. Screening is secondary, and rehabilitation is tertiary.

text: Question: The charge nurse in the long-term-care facility is preparing to deliver an in-service about the secondary level of health care for staff nurses. Which of the following information should the nurse include in the seminar?
A. Family planning and well-baby care.
B. Adult screening for blood pressure and cholesterol.
C. Family focused medical home and ambulatory care.
D. Rehabilitative programs such as sports medicine and orthopedic.
Correct answer: B. Adult screening for blood pressure and cholesterol.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:

Secondary prevention is screening and early diagnosis and treatment, such as adult blood pressure and cholesterol screening. Family planning and well-baby care are primary, and rehabilitation is tertiary.
